description: SilverFile course-scope rule corpus. Each rule cites the assignment (authoritative for scope) and/or a verified page of an IRS document listed in data/source_manifest.json. Logic for each rule id lives in src/rules.py; tests in tests/unit/test_decision_table.py.

rules.title: Form 1040-SR eligibility
rules.description: The taxpayer must have been born before January 2, 1961. On a joint return only one spouse needs to meet this. There is no income restriction.
rules.decision: eligible if taxpayer.dob < 1961-01-02, or filing_status == mfj and spouse.dob < 1961-01-02; otherwise out of scope (escalate).

rules.title: Filing status validation
rules.description: The chosen filing status must be one of the five statuses and consistent with the facts collected: single/head of household require not married at year end; joint/separate require married at year end; head of household requires a qualifying person; qualifying surviving spouse requires a spouse who died in 2023 or 2024 and a dependent child.
rules.decision: valid when the facts support the chosen status; inconsistent or unknown -> filing-status ambiguity escalation (R-HITL-05).

citations.section: Filing Status: Single, Married Filing Jointly
Head of Household; Qualifying Surviving Spouse

rules.title: Spouse died during the tax year
rules.description: A spouse who died during 2025 makes the filing status ambiguous (MFJ vs QSS vs Single) and also affects the line 12d age box. Always escalate to a human.

rules.title: Line 12d box count
rules.description: One box each for: taxpayer born before January 2, 1961; taxpayer blind; spouse born before January 2, 1961; spouse blind. Spouse boxes only on a joint return, or on a separate return when the spouse had no income, is not filing, and cannot be claimed as a dependent. No spouse boxes for head of household.
rules.decision: boxes computed deterministically from dates and yes/no answers; count read by the standard_deduction MCP tool.

rules.title: Standard Deduction Chart exceptions
rules.description: The chart does not apply if the taxpayer (or spouse on a joint return) can be claimed as a dependent, if a separately filing spouse itemizes, or if the taxpayer was a dual-status alien. All three are escalation conditions.

rules.title: Standard Deduction Chart amounts
rules.description: Base: $15,750 Single/MFS; $31,500 MFJ/QSS; $23,625 HOH. Each checked line 12d box adds $2,000 if unmarried and not a surviving spouse, otherwise $1,600.
rules.decision: computed by MCP tool standard_deduction; audited against a literal copy of the chart.

rules.title: Enhanced deduction for seniors
rules.description: Up to $6,000 per qualifying person (born before January 2, 1961, with a valid SSN; in this classroom system a fictional 900-series SSN). $12,000 if both spouses qualify on a joint return. Claimed on Schedule 1-A and carried to line 13b. Separate from the additional standard deduction on line 12d. Applies to tax years 2025-2028.

citations.section: What's New: Enhanced deduction for seniors

rules.title: Enhanced deduction: married must file jointly
rules.description: If married, the taxpayer must file jointly to claim the enhanced deduction; married filing separately gets $0.

citations.section: What's New: Enhanced deduction for seniors

rules.title: Enhanced deduction phaseout
rules.description: Reduced by 6% of MAGI above $75,000 ($150,000 joint), applied per qualifying individual, floored at zero. MAGI = Form 1040-SR line 11b plus Puerto Rico / Form 2555 / Form 4563 exclusions (none in scope, so MAGI = AGI).

rules.title: Social Security Benefits Worksheet
rules.description: Taxable benefits from provisional income (other income + tax-exempt interest + half of benefits, less certain Schedule 1 adjustments) against $25,000/$32,000 base and $34,000/$44,000 second-tier amounts (expressed on the worksheet as $9,000/$12,000 above the base). Married filing separately and living with spouse: 85% of line 7.

citations.section: Social Security Benefits Worksheet - Lines 6a and 6b

rules.title: Social Security ordering dependency
rules.description: The worksheet needs every other income line before it can run, and line 6b then feeds line 9 and AGI. The computation plan therefore computes 1z, 2a/2b, 3a/3b, 4a/4b, 5a/5b, 8 first, then 6b, then line 9, then 11a/11b.
rules.decision: enforced by the computation agent's dependency order and tested in tests/unit/test_computation_order.py.

rules.title: Social Security worksheet exceptions
rules.description: Repayments exceeding benefits (negative box 5), lump-sum elections for earlier years, and the Pub. 590-A / Pub. 915 cases are not handled by the in-scope worksheet.

rules.title: W-2 wages and withholding
rules.description: Box 1 (wages, tips, other compensation) of every W-2 is added for line 1a and carried to line 1z; box 2 (federal income tax withheld) is added for line 25a. Lines 1b-1i are not used by SilverFile (other wage types escalate as out of scope).

rules.title: 1099-INT interest
rules.description: Taxable interest (line 2b) = box 1 + box 3; tax-exempt interest (line 2a) = box 8; box 4 withholding goes to line 25b.

rules.title: 1099-DIV dividends
rules.description: Ordinary dividends (line 3b) = box 1a; qualified dividends (line 3a) = box 1b, a subset of 1a, never added again; exempt-interest dividends (box 12) go to line 2a; box 4 withholding goes to line 25b. Capital gain distributions (box 2a > 0) need line 7a and are escalated as capital gains.
rules.decision: aggregated by MCP tool aggregate_amounts; box 2a > 0 -> escalate.

rules.title: IRA distributions (lines 4a/4b)
rules.description: A 1099-R with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked and distribution code 7 is an IRA distribution: line 4a = box 1, line 4b = box 2a less any qualified charitable distribution. SilverFile fills 4a with the total even when fully taxable because the assignment table requires it (IRS instructions would leave 4a blank; see docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md A-14). Roth, rollover, nondeductible-basis (Form 8606) and other codes are out of scope.

rules.title: Qualified charitable distribution (QCD)
rules.description: If all or part of an IRA distribution is a QCD, enter the total on 4a, exclude the QCD from 4b, and check box 2 on line 4c. The taxpayer must have been at least 70 1/2 when the distribution was made; otherwise escalate.
rules.decision: QCD amount is a confirmed direct input; age check deterministic.

rules.title: Pensions and annuities (lines 5a/5b)
rules.description: A 1099-R without the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box, code 7, with a determined taxable amount: line 5a = box 1, line 5b = box 2a. SilverFile fills 5a with the total even when fully taxable (assignment table; docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md A-14).

rules.title: 1099-R taxable amount not determined
rules.description: Any 1099-R with box 2b 'taxable amount not determined' checked needs the Simplified Method or General Rule, neither of which is in scope. Escalate regardless of other information.
rules.decision: checked -> escalate (form_1099r_2b). A reviewer may only refer the case or correct a misread checkbox; it cannot be made eligible.

rules.title: 1099-R distribution code
rules.description: Only distribution code 7 (normal distribution) is in scope. Early distributions, rollovers (G/H), Roth codes (Q/T/J), death benefits and others need rules outside the assignment.

rules.title: SSA-1099 mapping
rules.description: Box 5 (net benefits) of all SSA-1099s is line 6a and worksheet line 1; box 6 (voluntary federal income tax withheld) goes to line 25b.

rules.title: Withholding classification
rules.description: Line 25a: W-2 box 2. Line 25b: 1099-INT/DIV/R box 4 and SSA-1099 box 6. Line 25c: other forms (W-2G, 8959, K-1, 1042-S) - none are in scope, so 25c is $0.

rules.title: Schedules 1, 2 and 3 direct inputs
rules.description: Schedule 1 line 10 -> line 8; Schedule 1 line 26 -> line 10; Schedule 2 line 3 -> line 17; Schedule 3 line 8 -> line 20; Schedule 2 line 21 -> line 23; Schedule 3 line 15 -> line 31. The taxpayer enters these totals directly; each is recorded as direct user input. Schedule 1 line 21 (student loan interest) is collected so the Social Security worksheet can use lines 11-20, 23 and 25 only.

rules.title: Total payments
rules.description: Line 25d = 25a + 25b + 25c; line 26 = estimated payments from intake; line 33 = 25d + 26 + 32 (line 32 = refundable credits; only Schedule 3 line 15 is in scope).

rules.title: Overpayment or amount owed
rules.description: Line 34 = line 33 - line 24 when positive; line 37 = line 24 - line 33 when positive.

rules.title: Adjusted gross income
rules.description: Line 11a = line 9 - line 10; line 11b repeats line 11a.

rules.title: Deductions and taxable income
rules.description: Line 14 = 12e + 13a + 13b (13a QBI is out of scope, $0); line 15 = 11b - 14, not less than zero.

rules.title: Tax on taxable income
rules.description: Tax Table for taxable income under $100,000 (row-midpoint method, verified against every printed row), Tax Computation Worksheet at $100,000 or more.

rules.title: Qualified dividends tax method
rules.description: When line 3a is positive, line 16 uses the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet so qualified dividends are taxed at 0/15/20% rather than as ordinary income. The assignment's 'rate schedule' wording is interpreted to include this worksheet (docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md A-11).

citations.section: Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet

rules.title: Total tax
rules.description: Lines 17-24 using direct Schedule 2/3 inputs; line 19 credits only as a direct input when dependents are claimed.

rules.title: Whole-dollar rounding
rules.description: All amounts are rounded to whole dollars (drop under 50 cents, raise 50-99 cents). When adding two or more amounts for one line, cents are kept and only the total is rounded.

rules.title: Independent audit checks
rules.description: The Review / Audit agent recomputes totals, checks 6b <= 6a (and <= 85% of 6a), 3a <= 3b, 4b <= 4a, 5b <= 5a, standard deduction against the literal chart, provenance completeness and scope before any human sees the return.
rules.decision: MCP tool verify_return plus provenance checks.

rules.title: User statement vs document conflict
rules.description: If the taxpayer's stated wages differ from the W-2 total by more than the larger of $1,000 or 10% (project tolerance), Intake asks one follow-up question. If the conflict remains, escalate.
rules.decision: MCP tool compare_amounts; unresolved after follow-up -> escalate (user_document_conflict).

rules.title: Document identity checks
rules.description: Every document must be for tax year 2025, show a fictional 900-series SSN, and belong to the taxpayer or spouse (SSN last four match). Otherwise ask the taxpayer (wrong year / wrong person) or reject the upload (real-looking SSN).
rules.decision: deterministic checks in the extraction aggregator and rules agent.

rules.title: Dependents
rules.description: Dependents need name, fictional SSN and relationship (assignment §3.1). The form has four dependent slots; more than four escalates. Credits for dependents (Schedule 8812) are not calculated; line 19 is only filled from a direct input.

citations.section: Dependents (if more than four, see instructions)

rules.title: Out-of-scope income and situations
rules.description: Itemized deductions (Schedule A); self-employment or business income (Schedule C, 1099-NEC); rental income (Schedule E); capital gains requiring Schedule D; digital assets; foreign income or accounts; amended or prior-year returns; state returns; more than four dependents; wages not on a W-2. Escalate to a human, never attempt.

rules.title: Escalation: out of scope
rules.description: Any out-of-scope item from §3.3 interrupts the graph for a human reviewer.

rules.title: Escalation: unresolved user/document conflict
rules.description: See R-CONFLICT-01.

rules.title: Escalation: advice request
rules.description: Requests for tax advice, planning or optimisation (e.g. Roth conversion, filing separately to pay less, deducting medications) are out of scope: explain the scope, note the question for a volunteer preparer, and escalate.

rules.title: Escalation: filing-status ambiguity
rules.description: Including a spouse who died during the tax year, an unsure taxpayer, or facts inconsistent with the chosen status.

rules.title: Escalation: financial exploitation or third-party pressure
rules.description: For example a refund routed to an account the taxpayer cannot describe or that is not in their name, or a third party answering for the taxpayer without stated authority. SilverFile notices and stops; it does not adjudicate.

rules.title: No tax advice
rules.description: Transcription and arithmetic are allowed; optimisation and planning are advice and are never given.

rules.title: Never file
rules.description: The output is a draft plus an audit record for a human. 'Submitted' in the dashboard means submitted internally for human review, never to the IRS.
rules.decision: no filing capability exists in the code.

rules.title: Never assert an unsourced amount
rules.description: Every monetary value on the draft carries a provenance record: a document box, a dated direct user input, a reviewer correction, or an MCP tool run over those.
rules.decision: enforced by return assembly; missing lineage blocks draft-ready.

rules.title: Fictional SSNs only
rules.description: Accept only nine-digit SSNs with a 900-999 prefix, formatted or unformatted, normalised to 9XX-XX-XXXX. Classroom constraint, not a real-world validity rule.
